Revenue to Plan (Section 6.3) fails for the three months ended October 31, 2026. Revenue was {{fact:32b5f800-7ba4-40ae-a06e-98552fb2dd87}} of the Approved Plan, below the required minimum of {{fact:97c5f746-53de-4edc-8b8d-533a44d4b33e}}. The borrower's October certificate reports the same figure, {{fact:76cd453d-92fa-4e7f-9576-e17ea7ae2ed6}}, and states it was not in compliance. Approved terms version 1 is the only version on file, and no amendments are waiting for approval. Searches of the documents found no waiver and no written update to the Approved Plan. I reran the test under version 1 and it still fails: {{fact:29c31cd6-7373-4876-b3d4-086110c21498}} against {{fact:ede80d2b-61a0-469a-9d54-d7722a8f477c}}, a shortfall of {{fact:0c782896-89e4-4b19-91b2-46d4a52a8fb5}} relative to the requirement. The September certificate also reported non-compliance with this covenant, so the shortfall goes back more than one period. Nothing found explains the failure, so it appears to be a real breach.

Revenue to Plan (Section 6.3) fails for the three months ended October 31, 2026. Revenue was {{fact:32b5f800-7ba4-40ae-a06e-98552fb2dd87}} of the Approved Plan, below the required minimum of {{fact:97c5f746-53de-4edc-8b8d-533a44d4b33e}}. The borrower's October certificate reports the same figure, {{fact:76cd453d-92fa-4e7f-9576-e17ea7ae2ed6}}, and states it was not in compliance. The approved terms in force are the only version on file, and no amendments are waiting for approval. Searches of the documents found no waiver and no written update to the Approved Plan. I reran the test under the approved terms and it still fails: {{fact:29c31cd6-7373-4876-b3d4-086110c21498}} against {{fact:ede80d2b-61a0-469a-9d54-d7722a8f477c}}, a shortfall of {{fact:0c782896-89e4-4b19-91b2-46d4a52a8fb5}} relative to the requirement. The September certificate also reported non-compliance with this covenant, so the shortfall did not begin in October. Nothing found explains the failure, so it appears to be a real breach.

Revenue reached {{fact:32b5f800-7ba4-40ae-a06e-98552fb2dd87}} of plan against a covenant floor of {{fact:97c5f746-53de-4edc-8b8d-533a44d4b33e}}. That leaves headroom of {{fact:ae43e3ef-1fea-4417-960e-f71e423237bb}}, so the covenant level is not being met rather than merely close. The revenue-below-plan and falling-headroom signals describe the same shortfall.

Revenue came in at {{fact:4bf4d2f4-2224-4f95-9d8b-41d59d1dd898}} of plan. For a SaaS borrower, that points to weaker bookings, churn or delayed renewals. This is the operating cause behind the revenue covenant shortfall, and it may also explain the steady erosion in cash headroom.

Revenue covenant headroom has slid each month: from {{fact:42050e4a-ce3c-4af0-ba42-72b6a00e7406}} in August, to {{fact:7811a1dd-1c93-4785-9b8d-f5db44b8c429}} in September, to {{fact:ae43e3ef-1fea-4417-960e-f71e423237bb}} in October. The shortfall began in September and deepened in October, so it is a worsening trend rather than a one-month miss.

Unrestricted cash of {{fact:29cd8d28-78a3-4c0b-a29d-b33eca788e0c}} remains comfortably above the {{fact:69ddefe1-73f7-4ffa-9ce8-bbaef95ad183}} minimum. However, headroom has declined steadily, from {{fact:49054f80-7d19-4d2e-a0c2-66cc7628c4cd}} to {{fact:8ce31a07-18b0-4706-ae13-cb74dd1b2656}} to {{fact:8d80b4d7-54c2-4f69-a386-50366ce31c62}}. Taken together with the revenue shortfall, this suggests cash burn is drawing down the liquidity cushion.
